mutation_class_covered: append (WRITER_APIS) and destroy (DESTRUCTIVE_APIS); a writer call that passes a scratch write_dir= / user_import_write_dir= is not an offender, because the write provably cannot reach the tracked tree
repair_mechanism: NavigationAPI gained write_dir=, CorpusLoader gained user_import_write_dir=, and both default to the historical behaviour. The 15 affected modules now either pass tmp_path or hand NavigationAPI a tempfile.mkdtemp() scratch directory, and the three idempotency helpers that used to shutil.rmtree tracked user_imports directories now wipe scratch state instead.
what_this_is: Every product/tests module that hands a path in the TRACKED product/results/ tree to an API that mutates or destroys it: the appenders (NavigationAPI/submit_feedback/export_feedback/save_map/save_meta) and the destructors (rmtree/unlink/remove/rmdir/removedirs/rename/replace). Such a fixture changes a committed file on every pytest run; core-lane.yml collects the tree with `git add -A`, so append-residue was once committed as a cycle's entire delta (run 39073545280, +20 lines) and rtree-residue deletes committed fixtures outright.
why_unfixed_is_not_excused: NOBODY - the unfixed remainder is EMPTY and MEASURED at 0, not asserted. Cycle 39082232157 pinned this at 38 lines across 14 modules and declined to fix them, because every one of those modules needs sentence_transformers/torch and could not be COLLECTED or EXECUTED in a bare environment; editing code that cannot run would have replaced a recorded defect with an unmeasured one. Cycle 39097705922 removed that premise (the eager `from sentence_transformers import ...` in product/app/navigation.py is now lazy, restoring all 18 modules to the collectible set), then repaired the whole class and demonstrated the repair empirically: running those 14 modules leaves `git status --porcelain product/results` empty, where before the repair the same run MODIFIED one tracked fixture and DELETED another.
